title: NIH Summer Internship Program (SIP)
sponsor: National Institutes of Health
pay_text: Monthly stipend based on school level, from $2,530 to $4,190 a month
who_text: U.S. citizens or permanent residents who are 18 by September 30, 2027 (17 is allowed for graduating seniors living within 40 miles of an NIH campus). Must be a graduating high school senior or enrolled at least half-time in college, graduate or professional school.
description: A full-time summer research job in an NIH lab, working with a scientist on biomedical, behavioral or health research. Most labs are on NIH campuses such as the main one in Bethesda, Maryland. The 2027 program runs May 10 to August 31, and you need to find your own housing.

title: Cancer Research Interns (CRI) Summer Program
sponsor: National Cancer Institute (NIH)
who_text: Undergraduate, graduate and medical students. The program is meant for students with little or no research experience.
description: A paid summer internship of up to 12 weeks at the National Cancer Institute. Interns explore cancer research, including lab science, clinical research, epidemiology and global health, with a mentor and career training.

title: Biomedical Engineering Summer Internship Program (BESIP)
sponsor: National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering (NIH)
who_text: Undergraduates at a U.S. college who will return to school for at least one more semester. The BME track needs three years of engineering, physical science or computer science study plus lab experience; the STEM track needs one year of study.
description: An in-person summer research internship in NIH labs in Bethesda, Maryland, for students interested in biomedical engineering. Interns work on a project picked from a list and join NIH career and training events. You apply through the NIH summer internship application.

title: NLM Data Science and Informatics (DSI) Scholars Program
sponsor: National Library of Medicine (NIH)
pay_text: Paid at NIH training stipend rates based on education and experience
who_text: U.S. citizens or permanent residents 18 by the start date (17 if living within 40 miles of an NIH campus) who are high school seniors or college students and have taken computer science, data science, math or similar courses.
description: An 8 to 12 week full-time summer internship using computers and data to answer questions in biology and health. Interns work one-on-one with a mentor at the National Library of Medicine in Bethesda, Maryland, and present at a summer poster day.

title: Science Undergraduate Laboratory Internships (SULI)
sponsor: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science
pay_text: $650 per week, plus travel reimbursement and possible housing support
who_text: U.S. citizens or permanent residents 18 or older by the start date who are full-time undergraduates or recent graduates, with at least 12 college credits (6 in STEM) and a 3.0 GPA.
description: A paid research internship at one of 17 Department of Energy national labs, working with a scientist or engineer. Terms run 10 weeks in the summer, fall or spring. The deadline shown is for the Spring 2027 term.

title: Community College Internships (CCI)
sponsor: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science
pay_text: $650 per week, plus travel reimbursement and possible housing support
who_text: U.S. citizens or permanent residents 18 or older by the start date who attend a community college full- or part-time, with at least 12 college credits (6 in STEM) and a 2.7 GPA (a waiver statement is needed under 3.0).
description: A paid 10-week technical internship for community college students at one of 17 Department of Energy national labs. Interns work on a project with a lab scientist or engineer. The deadline shown is for the Spring 2027 term; summer and fall terms are also offered.

title: Mickey Leland Energy Fellowship (MLEF)
sponsor: U.S. Department of Energy
pay_text: $7,500 for undergraduates and $8,500 for master's students for the 10 weeks
who_text: Full-time STEM students 18 or older at a U.S. college, at the associate, bachelor's or master's level. Undergraduates must be sophomores or higher with one full year done, and all need at least a 2.8 GPA.
description: A 10-week summer research internship at a Department of Energy national lab or DOE headquarters. Fellows work with a mentor on an energy research project and present it at a technical forum. The 2027 program runs June 7 to August 13.

title: NASA OSTEM Internships
sponsor: NASA
pay_text: Most interns get a stipend based on school level and session length
who_text: U.S. citizens at least 16 years old who are full- or part-time college students (undergraduate or graduate) with at least a 3.0 GPA. Recent graduates can apply for the three sessions right after graduating. STEM and non-STEM majors can apply.
description: Internships at NASA centers across the country, in science, engineering, and other fields. Interns work on real NASA projects with a mentor. The deadline shown is for Summer 2027; the Fall 2027 deadline is May 24, 2027.

title: NSF Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU)
sponsor: U.S. National Science Foundation
pay_text: Competitive stipends, often with help for housing, meals and travel
who_text: Undergraduates working toward an associate or bachelor's degree who are U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals or permanent residents. Each site may add its own rules.
description: NSF pays for hundreds of research programs at colleges, where small groups of students do real research with professors, mostly in the summer. You search the NSF directory of REU sites and apply to each site directly. Most summer sites have deadlines between January and March.

title: NIST Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship (SURF)
sponsor: National Institute of Standards and Technology
pay_text: $7,810 for the 11-week summer in 2026 ($710 per week), plus some housing and travel help
who_text: U.S. citizens or permanent residents at least 18 years old who are full-time undergraduates at a two-year or four-year U.S. college. First-year students and graduating seniors can apply.
description: A summer research fellowship in NIST labs in Gaithersburg, Maryland, or Boulder, Colorado, working with NIST scientists. For 2027, applications are expected to open in mid-October 2026 and close at the end of January 2027.

title: NIST Summer High School Intern Program (SHIP)
sponsor: National Institute of Standards and Technology
who_text: High school juniors or seniors with at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA who live within 50 miles of NIST in Gaithersburg, Maryland, or Boulder, Colorado, and can attend all seven weeks.
description: A seven-week unpaid summer research internship where high school students work on a project with NIST scientists and engineers. Families provide housing and transportation. For 2027, applications are expected to open in mid-October 2026 and close at the end of January 2027.

title: Science and Engineering Apprenticeship Program (SEAP)
sponsor: U.S. Navy, Office of Naval Research
pay_text: $4,000 for new interns, $4,500 for returning interns
who_text: U.S. citizens who are at least 16 by the internship start date, have finished 9th grade, and are enrolled in high school (graduating seniors can apply). Some labs accept permanent residents or dual citizens.
description: An eight-week summer internship where high school students do real research at a Navy lab with a scientist or engineer as a mentor. About 300 spots are spread across 38 labs around the country.

title: Naval Research Enterprise Internship Program (NREIP)
sponsor: U.S. Navy, Office of Naval Research
pay_text: $7,500 for new undergraduates, $9,000 returning, $11,500 for graduate students
who_text: U.S. citizens enrolled full-time at a four-year college who will have finished freshman year by the start, plus graduate students. Some labs accept permanent residents or two-year college students.
description: A 10-week summer research internship at one of 62 Navy labs across the country. College students work on Navy science and technology projects with a mentor.

title: Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Scholars Program
sponsor: Air Force Research Laboratory
pay_text: Weekly stipend by school level and site, for example $506.80 a week for high school students
who_text: U.S. citizens at least 16 by the deadline (18 for California sites) who are enrolled at least half-time in high school or college. Must work full-time in summer, get to the base daily, and pass a background check.
description: A paid summer internship at Air Force research sites, where upper-level high school students and college students work with AFRL scientists and engineers on research projects. Applications for Summer 2027 open October 12, 2026.

title: AEOP Internships (Army Educational Outreach Program)
sponsor: U.S. Army
pay_text: Educational stipend; amount depends on the lab location and program length
who_text: U.S. citizens or permanent residents at least 14 years old who are in high school or an undergraduate program, or finished one within the last 60 months. Some labs add their own age or other rules.
description: Paid research internships at Army research labs and partner university labs, mostly full-time for 6 to 10 weeks in summer. Interns must live close enough to commute, since housing and transportation are not provided. Deadlines vary by position.

title: Gains in the Education of Mathematics and Science (GEMS)
sponsor: U.S. Army
pay_text: No fee; in-person campers get a $125 per week educational stipend
who_text: Students in rising grades 5 through 12 who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents. The virtual camp is for 6th to 8th graders.
description: A free summer STEM camp held at Army research labs, with hands-on lab activities in areas like biology, chemistry and engineering. Camps are grouped by grade and run in several states, plus a virtual camp for middle schoolers. Applications are usually due in March or April.

title: Youth Conservation Corps (YCC)
sponsor: National Park Service
pay_text: At least the state or federal minimum wage, whichever is higher
who_text: Youth ages 15 through 18 who are permanent residents of the United States and can commute to the park or site every day.
description: A paid summer job, usually 8 to 10 weeks, doing outdoor work at national parks, forests, wildlife refuges and fish hatcheries, like building trails and restoring streams. Most programs are day programs near home, so you get yourself there each day. Contact a participating park to apply.

title: Smithsonian Internships
sponsor: Smithsonian Institution
pay_text: Some internships include a stipend; each listing says whether it does
who_text: Anyone at least 14 years old. Most internships are for college or graduate students, but some are for high school students. Each listing gives its own age, school and citizenship rules.
description: More than 1,500 internships across Smithsonian museums and research centers, in fields from art history to zoology. You browse the listings and apply to the ones that match your goals. Deadlines vary by internship.

title: Idaho National Laboratory Internships
sponsor: Idaho National Laboratory (U.S. Department of Energy)
pay_text: Wage based on credits earned and degree program
who_text: Full-time students at an accredited high school or college, enrolled the semester before and after the internship, with at least a 3.0 GPA.
description: Paid internships at a Department of Energy lab in Idaho, mostly in fields like nuclear engineering, chemistry, computer science and physics, plus business and communications. Interns work with a mentor, and many internships offer travel and housing help.

title: Argonne College Bound Research Program
sponsor: Argonne National Laboratory (U.S. Department of Energy)
pay_text: $500 per week
who_text: Graduating seniors from a local Illinois high school who will attend college full-time in the fall, are 18 by the start, are U.S. citizens or permanent residents, and have at least a 3.75 unweighted GPA.
description: A full-time summer research job at Argonne National Laboratory for students between high school graduation and college. You work in a lab or office alongside scientists and engineers. Students arrange their own daily transportation.

title: Fermilab PRISM (Program for Research, Innovation, and STEM Mentorship)
sponsor: Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory (U.S. Department of Energy)
pay_text: $500 weekly
who_text: U.S. citizens who will be high school seniors in the 2027-2028 school year or who graduate high school in 2027.
description: A paid four-week summer school at Fermilab, a physics lab near Chicago. Students explore particle physics, quantum science, engineering and artificial intelligence through hands-on activities, talks and lab tours. The 2027 program runs July 12 to August 6.

title: Fermilab VALOR JROTC Internship
sponsor: Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory (U.S. Department of Energy)
pay_text: $18 per hour
who_text: Illinois JROTC high school juniors, seniors and recent graduates.
description: A paid six-week summer internship at Fermilab in Batavia, Illinois, for JROTC students. Interns give technical support to an experiment or support group under a Fermilab employee. The 2027 program runs June 28 to August 6.

title: CDC Museum Disease Detective Camp
sponsor: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
who_text: High school students in the summer before their junior or senior year who are at least 16 on the first day of camp.
description: A free one-week day camp at CDC headquarters in Atlanta where students learn public health by acting as disease detectives, with mock outbreaks, lab sessions and talks from CDC scientists. Campers provide their own housing and transportation. Information about 2027 is expected in January 2027.

title: CDC Museum Public Health Academy Online Summer Course
sponsor: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
who_text: High school students in the summer before their junior or senior year who are at least 16 on the first day of the course.
description: A free one-week online course from the CDC Museum about how CDC works, public health, and epidemiology (the study of how diseases spread). Information about 2027 is expected in January 2027.

title: CDC Student Worksite Experience Program (SWEP)
sponsor: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
who_text: High school, college and graduate students.
description: An unpaid volunteer program where students work on CDC projects to gain real work experience in public health, for up to 180 days a year. You apply by emailing a resume and an interest form.

title: CDC John R. Lewis Undergraduate Public Health Scholars Program
sponsor: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
pay_text: Stipend set by each partner program (for example, $3,400 at the University of Pittsburgh)
who_text: Undergraduate students and recent graduates interested in public health. Each of the seven partner programs sets its own rules.
description: A summer program that introduces college students to public health and health equity through seven partner schools and organizations. You pick a partner program and apply on its website. Applications open each fall.

title: DHS HS-POWER Summer Internship
sponsor: U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Science and Technology Directorate
pay_text: $800 per week for undergraduates, plus a $500 per week housing allowance
who_text: U.S. citizens 18 or older who are undergraduate or graduate students in homeland security related STEM fields or social sciences.
description: A 10-week summer research internship starting in June, where each student is paired with a mentor at DHS headquarters, a DHS agency or a DHS lab. Interns work on research that supports national security.

title: USDA Internship Program
sponsor: U.S. Department of Agriculture
who_text: U.S. citizens at least 18 years old. Being a current student or college graduate is not required.
description: An unpaid, in-person internship at USDA headquarters in Washington, D.C., helping with research, data, communications and outreach. The Spring 2027 group runs January 25 to April 30, 2027, and interns arrange their own housing.
